title: Edge ACK lag causing transient unmetered spike and quota mismatches
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
We observed intermittent bursts of unmetered consumption after network partitions between edge proxies and central metering. When the edge proxy falls back to optimistic ACK behavior (acknowledging requests before receiving central debit confirmation), the local accounting window allows a short period where requests are served without being debited. This leads to a transient spike of tokens served beyond the org/key quota and causes downstream billing reconciliation mismatches.

Scope:
- Affects hosted and dedicated edge proxies that implement ACK pipelining during control-plane outages.
- Observed across multiple orgs but amplifies for high-concurrency routes.

Why this is important:
- Causes measurable revenue leakage and customer confusion when usage shows higher runtime but billing shows later reconciliation deductions or chargebacks.
- Can trigger quota exhaustion on central side resulting in sudden throttles for unrelated keys when eventual reconciliation applies debits retroactively.

Expected behavior:
- Edge should never permanently grant more allowance than central policy permits. During control-plane unavailability the edge may queue/deny, or optimistically allow but track promised debits and reconcile without creating an overage window that is visible to other tenants or causing billing drift.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure an edge proxy instance with optimistic ACK enabled and point it at a staging org with per-key quota of 1000 req/min.
2) Run a sustained concurrent traffic generator (200 concurrent connections, steady ramp) for 90s to reach steady-state serving from edge cache.
3) Simulate transient partition by blocking network between the proxy and central metering for 12s.
4) Observe that the edge continues to ACK and serve requests locally during the partition; central metering receives bursts when connectivity returns.

5) Inspect per-key counters in central metering and compare to edge logs: edge shows allowed requests without immediate debit; central shows backlog debits applied later, creating a window where served tokens were not accounted for in real-time.
6) Repeat with multiple routes and orgs to see amplification and cross-org reconciliation effects when central aggregate quotas hit limits after backlog drain.
investigation_notes:
2025-02-11 | Owen Ramirez: Collected proxy logs for three incidents; found 'ACK_SENT' before 'DEBIT_CONFIRMED' in edge trace sequences. The edge increments local consumption counter immediately on ACK.
Action: added additional logging around pending_debits queue size.

2025-02-14 | Maya Patel: Reproduced locally using a network proxy (toxiproxy) to introduce 10-15s partitions. Confirmed pattern: local allowance increases, central debit backlog drains on reconnection causing sudden central debit spikes.

2025-02-18 | SRE (Lena Vo): Observed that throttles happen when backlog debits push central per-route aggregate over its soft-limit causing cascading failures on other tenant served by same shard. SRE recommends a quick mitigation: cap local optimistic allowance to a small configurable window per-key (current default is unlimited during partition).

2025-02-22 | Product (Anika Singh): Customer-facing impact: some customers saw invoice adjustments and elevated support tickets. PM requests fast patch and rollout with telemetry to quantify leakage volume.

2025-02-24 | Engineering: Reviewed edge proxy code path 'serve_optimistic' and discovered it maintains two counters: local_allowed and promised_debits. Bug: promised_debits were not included when enforcing local_allowed max, so local_allowed could exceed policy during sustained partitions.
observed_metrics: edge_unacked_allowed_rate: spike to 4x baseline during partitions
pending_debits_queue_length: peaked at 18k items on one proxy
billing_recon_drift: sample orgs showed 2-7% extra served tokens not matched to timely billing within a 24h window
impact_assessment: Revenue risk: medium-high for high-volume tenants; small tenants see negligible absolute loss but high relative variance.
Customer experience: high — unexpected throttles and invoice adjustments create trust issues.
Operational risk: high — central shards can be overloaded when multiple proxies flush backlogs simultaneously.
proposed_fixes: Short-term (fast patch): Introduce a hard cap on optimistic local allowance per-key during control-plane partition. Default cap: 5% of configured quota or 1000 tokens, whichever is smaller. Add feature flag to disable optimistic ACK entirely per-deployment.
Medium-term: Ensure promised_debits are counted against enforcement path in the edge so local_allowed = min(local_enforcement_budget, quota - promised_debits).

Long-term: Implement distributed backpressure across proxies for a shared shard via lease-based coordination so reconnection flushes are staggered to avoid central debit bursts. Also add a central 'replay-scheduler' to smooth backlog consumption.
Telemetry: Emit 'optimistic_cap_hit' and 'pending_debits_drain' events to console with per-proxy shard tags; add alert when pending_debits_queue_length > 1000.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy fast patch to staging edge fleet with cap config and verbose logging. Run soak for 48h with synthetic partition tests.
2) Canary deploy to 5% of production proxies in 'non-critical' regions and monitor pending_debits metrics and central shard load for 72h.
3) If canary stable, ramp to 50% then 100% over 48h windows. Maintain support on-call during ramp.
4) After stabilization, merge medium-term enforcement change and run extended integration tests with multi-proxy partition scenarios before rolling out.
5) Coordinate with Billing team to run reconciliation jobs for impacted orgs and notify customers if adjustments are required.
qa_checks: Automated: unit tests for edge accounting logic including promised_debits interaction; fuzz tests with randomized partition durations up to 60s.
Integration: toxiproxy network partition scenarios with 10k token/min traffic; assert central debit burst < 1.5x baseline after patch.
Load: simulate 100 proxies simultaneously reconnecting and ensure central shard CPU < 70% and debit rate remains within configured throttling thresholds.
